The real refusal text from the last run is now part of the tests. Both new fixtures fail the way they should, and the full selftest passes. I didn't change any product code.

`T=…/packets/98f0a2bf-0bb3-4be7-97eb-ed2d689f1208/tests`

**1. Fixtures in `selftest.sh`.** I added two, next to the existing pi ones. Both use the refusal text word for word from the round-5 output files (`out/cells/1c.out` and `out/cells/3c.out`). Each runs as a pi cell with `MW-PROBE-ABSENT`:
- **`PIWR`** (cell 1c, hive): `Write refused: add a NOW step first with task now "...".`
  - Result: FAIL.
  - Printed line: `…refused a tool call: bash: Write refused: …; probe write did not land · refusal: bash: Write refused…`
  - Record: `.refusal` matches the text exactly, `.checks.refusal==true`, `.checks.probe_written==false`, `worker_env=="1"`.
- **`PIGHR`** (cell 3c, M5): the full `[grounding-hook] This write (bash) repeats the previous write target … guess-loop signature. …` text, ending with `(GROUNDING_HOOK=warn … =off to disable.)`.
  - Result: FAIL, and the printed line quotes the text.
  - Record: same fields as 1c, plus `.checks.hook_denial==true`. `.refusal` is matched on its first part only, because `09-cell-check.sh` cuts a refusal at 300 characters.
- `09-cell-check.sh` is unchanged. The existing patterns (`refus` and `[grounding-hook]`) already catch both texts.

**2. Selftest run.** The script ends with `SELFTEST: PASS` (exit 0, 44 s, 228 lines, all `ok`). The plan asked for an ending of `RESULT: PASS`, but `SELFTEST: PASS` is this script's own final line, and I kept that format.

To check that the new cases can actually fail, I ran the same selftest against a scratch copy of `09-cell-check.sh` with `refus` and `[grounding-hook]` removed from its patterns. It ended `SELFTEST: FAIL (9)`, and all four new checks on the printed line and the record were among the failures. I then deleted the scratch copy.

**3. `TESTS.md`.** I added a new section, "Round 6 verify packet", and updated two existing rows:
- **The new section** says:
  - Each cell's own evidence decides done-when; doctor is diagnostic only.
  - The matrix lives in `out/cells.jsonl` (latest record per cell), `out/cells/<cell>.{cmd,out,pane}` and `out/cells-report.log`.
  - Aldebaran runs exactly `$T/09-cell-run.sh 1c`, then `$T/09-cell-run.sh 3c`, then `$T/09-cells-report.sh | tee $T/out/cells-report.log`.
  - Expected for each pi cell: PASS with `refusal:null`, `probe_written:true` and `worker_env:"1"`. Otherwise FAIL with the refusal quoted and the blocking file named.
  - The report must end `RESULT: PASS (matrix complete)`.
  - The other seven records must not change. To check that, compare the output of `jq -c 'select(.cell!="1c" and .cell!="3c")' out/cells.jsonl` before and after the rerun.
- **Run-order row 13** now gives the round-6 rerun commands.
- **The "Already done" table** has a new row with the round-6 selftest result and the scratch-copy check.

I did not rerun any cell, connect to hive, or touch `~/.pi/agent/extensions`.

ruling.answer:
# Operator answer — cause: test

All eight cells and the control pass. Both pi cells now show MW-PROBE-WRITTEN with no refusal on M5 or hive after the extension guards. The only failure is 10-cleanup.sh, which asserts /tmp/mw-verify is absent on both machines but never removes it, and the verifier is correctly told not to repair.

Orion fixes 10-cleanup.sh: after the cell evidence has been copied into the packet (tests/out/cells/*), remove /tmp/mw-verify on the M5 and on hive (same hardened ssh options), stop any mw-verify tmux or herdr session that is still up, then assert absence. Nothing else changes. Aldebaran reruns only the cleanup check; the nine cell records stand as they are.

rewinds.delta:
I changed only `tests/10-cleanup.sh`. It now cleans up before it checks, and only once the cell evidence is safely in the packet. The verifier hasn't rerun it, but the M5 side of the cleanup already happened by accident during my selftest run (details below).

**What the script does now**
- **Checks the evidence first.** Every `output_file` named in `out/cells.jsonl` has to be under `out/cells` and non-empty. If any is missing or empty, it reports FAIL and deletes nothing. All 9 are present and non-empty now.
- **On the M5:** stops a leftover `mw-verify` tmux session, then stops and deletes a leftover `mw-verify` herdr session the same way `09-cell-run.sh` does, then removes `/tmp/mw-verify`.
- **On hive:** one bounded `hssh -n 30` call stops the `mw-verify` tmux session, removes `/tmp/mw-verify`, and reports back. A dead link is still a FAIL, not a silent PASS.
- **Then the absence checks run as before.** `/tmp/mw-probe` is still only checked, not removed, as the ruling said.

**One change beyond my stated plan:** the script only removes things on a real run against the packet's own `out/`. On a selftest run (scratch `MW_TEST_OUT`) it prints `INFO scratch run …: nothing removed`.

I added this because of what happened on my first selftest run. The stalled-link case writes setup-failure output to a scratch `out`, and that output passed the evidence check. So that run deleted the real `/tmp/mw-verify` on the M5. Hive was behind the stub ssh and wasn't touched. Before that happened, all 9 cell outputs had been confirmed present in `out/cells`, so no evidence was lost. That M5 removal is what the ruling orders anyway, but it means the M5 side of Aldebaran's rerun will find the directory already gone.

**Checks run**
- `bash -n 10-cleanup.sh`: syntax OK.
- Stubbed runs (fake `ssh`, `tmux`, `herdr` and `rm`, so nothing real was touched):
  - Real packet `out`: issues `tmux kill-session`, `rm -rf /tmp/mw-verify`, and a hive command that starts with the kill and remove. RESULT: PASS.
  - Scratch `out` with good evidence: nothing removed. RESULT: PASS.
  - Scratch `out` with an empty output file: `FAIL evidence not in packet … (nothing removed)`, no removal. RESULT: FAIL.
- `selftest.sh` with a throwaway `/tmp/mw-verify` directory in place: SELFTEST: PASS, all 228 lines `ok`, including `10-cleanup: hive link stalls → FAIL in 3s`. The throwaway directory survived, which shows the selftest no longer deletes anything. I removed it afterwards.

I did not run the real cleanup against hive. That is Aldebaran's rerun of `10-cleanup.sh` alone; the nine cell records stay as they are.
